articles.title: Bluetti’s Sora 500 solar panel is incredibly powerful for its size
articles.summary: Bluetti’s Sora 500 can’t compete with the Zoupw 480W and Jackery SolarSage 500 X in terms of raw output, price, and weight, but it wins handily in portability.
articles.body: We don’t review many solar panels at The Verge, but the tech inside Bluetti’s incredibly portable Sora 500 panel makes it worth a deeper look. The new N-Type panels made by Bluetti and others give you more bang for the buck, pound, and square inch. That’s a big deal for vanlifers like me who depend upon these beefy portable solar panels to extend off-grid stays. In real-world testing, I saw Bluetti’s 500W panel deliver 509W to my van’s power station, allowing me to generate over 800W when combined with the three sad 140W monocrystalline solar panels I have installed on top of my van. That kind of stationary output is fantastic. I typically consume about 1.6kWh a day, so this array lets me add a full day’s worth of charge in only two hours. I just wish that Bluetti had made the Sora 500 bifacial like Jackery and newcomer Zoupw did with their even lighter, high-wattage, portable, N-Type panels designed to maximize output in less than ideal conditions. The Sora 500 is priced at €849 in Europe — it isn’t being sold in the US yet. Bluetti spokesperson Ellen Lee tells me that the company wants to bring it to the US market but it’s “currently navigating some shifting regional policies and trade dynamics.” Things that Zoupw and Jackery managed to sort out already. [Product: Bluetti Sora 500 solar panel | Bluetti’s single-sided Sora 500 panel uses TOPCon (Tunnel Oxide Passivated Contact) cells, an N-Type technology which is replacing older PERC (Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell) tech. Compared to PERC, TOPCon panels do better in low-light, deal with high temperatures better, and degrade more slowly. TOPCon panels can achieve higher efficiencies (often ~23–25 percent) compared to typical PERC panels (~20–23 percent), depending on implementation. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: All these advantages mean that you’ll get more for your money, as soon as you unfurl all 12 panels of the Sora 500 and over their extended lifetime. The panel also features an IP67 resistance to dust and water and an ETFE coating that makes it easier to wipe away dirt that interferes with solar intake. [Image: Lightweight portables are no match for gusts of wind, this one was about 10 - 12 knots. In my mid-March testing in the south of France at an altitude of about 600 meters, I was regularly seeing the Sora 500 delivering above its rated output, measuring as much as 509W on a cool and cloudless day. It also does a good job of handling the sun being partially shaded. For example, on a very sunny day when the 12 individual panels that comprise the Sora 500 were producing over 500W, the output dropped to 412W when partially shading one corner panel, and 390W when partially shading the right-most two. Partially shading the four panels just to the right of center dropped the output to 276W. The output from the Sora 500 dropped dramatically when I blocked the center four panels, falling to just 50W. That’s likely because I choked off the entire array by severing the connection between all four parallel zones. Bluetti uses a half-cut cell design and a 3-series, 4-parallel (3S4P) circuit architecture for the Sora 500. This results in multiple independent power zones by dividing the cells into smaller halves and distributing them across four parallel power paths. It helps to prevent a single shaded area from becoming a bottleneck for the entire panel, like you see with cheaper panels. Unfortunately, Bluetti chose to cover the back of its panels with fabric and a complex system of kickstands and straps. By comparison, the Zoupw 480W and Jackery SolarSage 500 X N-Type panels are bifacial, meaning they can also collect ambient light from the back of the panels when placed on reflective surfaces like snow, sand, concrete, and, to a lesser extent, grass. I haven’t tested these panels myself, but I’ve seen unconfirmed user reports claiming to have pushed the Zoupw beyond 525W of output. Importantly, both panels also weigh just 22lb (10kg), making them even lighter than the 28.4lb (12.9kg) Bluetti Sora 500. And while weight is an important enabler of portability, I should note that these things tend to fly away when the wind picks up. Fortunately, the Bluetti panel I’ve been testing has tie-down points for gusty days. All three panels are much lighter than the reliable 400W PERC monster from EcoFlow that I’ve been hauling around for the last four years. It weighs 35.3lbs (16kg) and is still available to buy for $599. For vanlifers, the Bluetti Sora 500 absolutely dominates when it comes time to pack the panel away into an RV, van, or closet. The Zoupw and Jackery use standard 4-section or 6-section “slab” folds, while Bluetti uses a 12-section grid fold, allowing it to collapse into a much smaller, briefcase-like package. Even then, the 3.3-inch thick folded Bluetti is thinner than both the 3.35-inch thick Zoupw panel and 3.82-inch Jackery. Conversely, the Sora 500 can be a pain in the ass to set up due to all the hinges and straps needed to support so many segments. It’s a puzzle I managed to mostly master after the third installation, but repositioning the panel to follow the sun throughout the day is a lesson in patience. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Without official US pricing for the Sora 500 panel, it’s hard to do a direct price-per-watt comparison with the $649.99 Zoupw 480W and $999 (often on sale for $799) Jackery SolarSage 500 X. However, if we strip the European VAT from its €849 price tag and convert it, the Sora 500 works out to about $820. While that’s competitive, it still leaves the Zoupw 480W with the best price-per-watt performance in this class. Bluetti’s Sora 500 can’t compete with the Zoupw 480W and Jackery SolarSage 500 X in terms of weight, but it wins handily in terms of Watts per square inch when folded down. It’s the only 500W panel that effectively disappears into a small closet or under a van bench. As such, it justifies its price premium for anyone like me who has limited space to store an extra solar panel they only need to deploy occasionally. --- Specs: Sora 500 panel * Unfolded: 100 × 45.1 × 0.1 in / 2541 × 1146.6 × 3 mm * Folded: 22.4 × 17.5 × 3.3 in / 570 × 445 × 85 mm * Weight: 28.4 lbs / 12.9 kg * Panels: 12x TOPCon * Conversion Efficiency: up to 25 percent * Voltage at Pmax (Vmp):40.92V * Current at Pmax (Imp): 12.22A * Open Circuit Voltage (Voc): 49.1V * Short Circuit Current (Isc): 13.31A * Operating Temperature: -13°F to 149°F / -25°C to 65°C * Best Working Temperature: 77°F / 25°C * 1.5m MC4 to XT60 cable included in box --- Photography by Thomas Ricker / The Verge

articles.title: DJI’s latest power station is proof that good things come in mini packages
articles.summary: DJI’s Power 1000 Mini power station is the smallest 1kWh power station that money can currently buy.
articles.body: As an avid vanlifer, I have to carefully curate everything I carry in order to eke out every square inch of storage I can to support life off the grid for weeks at a time. That’s why I jumped at the chance to review DJI’s latest power station. The DJI Power 1000 Mini is almost half the size of the original DJI Power 1000 released two years ago with the same 1kWh battery capacity. And from my calculations, it’s also the smallest 1kWh power station from the major brands that money can currently buy. DJI’s little power station also has a few tricks up its sleeve, including a built-in retractable USB-C cable, a light that can be controlled remotely, an integrated MPPT controller that turns it into a solar generator, and the option to fast-charge off my van’s alternator when wired up to the starter battery. Hoozah! I found myself using the little DJI power station far more than expected in my two months of testing, despite traveling with a giant 8kWh battery system. The Power 1000 Mini is so small that I don’t hesitate to grab it whenever I need to power a projector for an outdoor movie night, keep my Starlink Mini internet running in a field, or power an air compressor to inflate my tires after leaving a sandy beach. The €579 / £449 Power 1000 Mini’s diminutive size does come with a few tradeoffs — dongles, ugh! — but I think DJI has struck an excellent balance between portability, versatility, and power. Right now, it’s unclear if it’ll get approved for sale in the US because “the application for authorization is still pending,” according to DJI spokesperson Daisy Kong. [Product: DJI Power 1000 Mini power station | Most people still think of DJI as a drone company, but the Chinese tech giant has branched out into several product categories, where it’s introduced real innovation. For example, the incredibly small and powerful Avinox e-bike drive system it developed has radically transformed what mountain bikers expect in terms of performance. Similarly, the DJI Power 1000 Mini resets expectations about how large a 1kWh power station should be. Just look at how it stacks up to the competition. [Image: Despite shrinking the footprint, DJI couldn’t do much with the weight, but most of that can be attributed to the industry settling on long-lasting LFP batteries. Some of DJI’s space savings are the result of using a less powerful inverter. On paper, DJI says the Power 1000 Mini can produce a continuous 800W of AC output (with a 1000W peak). That’s enough to power appliances like a small microwave or Instant Pot, but not a hair dryer set to max or power tools at a job site. For comparison, EcoFlow’s 1kWh Delta 2 and Anker’s Solix C1000 both offer 1800W of continuous output. In my testing, the Power 1000 Mini could power my 800W water boiler and, surprisingly, even my Nespresso coffee machine, which can briefly pull as much as 1200W. But it can’t power them simultaneously unless the power station is plugged into an AC wall jack. Then its bypass mode kicks in to deliver as much as 2200W of output to my 240V European model, which drops to 1440W for 120V US models. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: Whenever I exceeded its maximums, the Power 1000 Mini shut down gracefully with an “overload” message on the display, and a more detailed error report in the DJI Home app. It cleared with a simple on/off toggle of the power station. DJI’s power station also saves space by relying upon an SDC (Smart DC) connector to add I/O to the unit. By plugging in a variety of dongles, the SDC port can transform into a 12V barrel jack output or an MC4 connector for up to 400W of solar panel input. [Image: It’s grab-and-go portable. Uniquely, DJI also sells an SDC Power Car Battery Charging Cable that you can snake up to your car’s starter battery to charge the Power 1000 Mini at up to 400W while driving. That’s over three times faster than charging off your car’s 12V cigarette lighter socket, meaning you can take the Power 1000 Mini from empty to full in just over two hours of driving. I did not have an opportunity to test this. Naturally, this DJI battery also offers several proprietary SDC adapters that will charge DJI’s drones faster than any other power station on the market. If you’re already big into DJI gear then getting one of their power stations is pretty much a no-brainer. One of the best features of the Power 1000 Mini is the integrated 100W USB-C cable that retracts with a tug and magnetically folds into place. I like that it’s long enough to reach a table top when the power station is on the ground. I dislike that it, and the unit’s integrated USB-C jack, don’t support 140W like DJI’s original Power 1000. Fortunately, both USB-C jacks are bidirectional, so they can also be used to charge the mini DJI battery. Power stations have had lights integrated since forever, and can be very useful at the end of an all-day shoot when you’re trying to pack up. I like that I can remotely trigger it from the app while I’m still in bed. That way I can illuminate the van just enough for a little late-night spelunking while my wife is asleep. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: I gotta say, I wasn’t expecting a 1kWh battery to be so useful while traveling around southern Europe over the last several weeks. I’ve used many similarly specced power stations before, but their size never made it a grab-and-go device, causing me to carry a few smaller, but very capable, power banks instead. DJI’s Power 1000 Mini changes the equation for me, and anyone else that values portability and adaptability over raw power. --- Specs: DJI Power 1000 Mini Battery & Performance * Capacity: 1008 Wh (~1 kWh). * Chemistry: Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4). * Cycle Life: Rated to retain at least 80% of its original capacity after 4,000 complete charge cycles. * Output Power: Delivers 800W of continuous power, with a maximum rating of 1000W (and up to 1200W in boosted output modes). Ports & Connectivity * AC Output: Features 2 AC sockets in regions like the EU, UK, and Australia, or 4 AC sockets in the US and Japan. * Retractable USB-C Cable: Features a built-in, magnetically secured, and bidirectional USB-C cable that supports up to 100W fast charging. * Standard USB-C: One standard 100W USB-C port. * USB-A: Two standard 12W USB-A ports. * SDC Port: One proprietary DJI SDC port that supports up to 400W input (9-28V) and 300W output. * Smart Tech: Includes Bluetooth 5.0 and Wi-Fi for monitoring and control via the DJI app. Recharging * Speed: Capable of recharging from 0% to 80% in approximately 58 minutes, and reaching a full charge in roughly 75 minutes. * Methods: Can be recharged via AC wall outlets, USB-C, solar panels (up to 400W using the built-in MPPT module), or car alternators (up to 400W via the SDC port). Design & Dimensions * Weight: Approximately 11.5 kg (25.4 lbs). * Dimensions: 314 mm x 212 mm x 216 mm (12.4 x 8.3 x 8.5 inches). * Extra Features: Includes a built-in LED light with an SOS flashing mode, UPS mode for seamless backup power during outages, and an integrated carrying handle. --- Photography by Thomas Ricker / The Verge

articles.title: Sony CEO says PS5 no longer needs aggressive marketing as console enters later years
articles.summary: Gaming News: Sony is changing its strategy for the PlayStation 5 as the console moves deeper into the later part of its life cycle. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki said the.
articles.body: Sony is changing its strategy for the PlayStation 5 as the console moves deeper into the later part of its life cycle. Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki said the company is no longer focused on “aggressively” selling the PS5, arguing that the console has reached a stage where the company can put more attention on earning money from its existing players. “We are in the latter half of the life cycle for a PlayStation console,” Hiroki Totoki said in an interview with the Wall Street Journal in August this year. “That means that we do not need to ‘aggressively sell’ the console today,” he added.Sony says PS5 is now in the latter half of its life cycleThe shift comes nearly six years after the PlayStation 5 launched in November 2020. According to Totoki, Sony’s focus is now moving from selling more consoles to increasing recurring revenue from its large PlayStation user base.During the WSJ interview, Totoki said Sony does not need to push PS5 sales as aggressively as it did earlier in the console's life. Instead, Sony is looking at ways to generate more recurring revenue from people who already use PlayStation products and services.Totoki pointed to PlayStation Plus as an important part of that strategy. He said the service now has more than 125 million monthly active users, making its existing customer base a major opportunity for Sony.PlayStation Plus becomes more important for SonySony's comments suggest that services and subscriptions are becoming increasingly important to the PlayStation business as the PS5 matures. Rather than relying only on new console sales, the company wants to increase the value it gets from its existing users. PlayStation Plus offers access to online multiplayer, games and other benefits across its subscription plans.The comments also come at a time when Sony is dealing with changes across the PlayStation business, including higher hardware prices and growing debate around digital games.PS5 price increases and physical games debate continueSony increased the prices of the PS5, PS5 Pro and PlayStation Portal in several markets in April 2026, citing continued cost pressures.At the same time, the company has faced criticism from some players over its plans to reduce its reliance on physical game discs. Sony's chief financial officer Lin Tao said in July that the company would “cautiously move forward” with ending physical discs, pointing to the growing digitisation of content.Sony has also faced a class-action lawsuit over how digital game purchases are presented to consumers. The company has argued that consumers should not assume they permanently own digital games in the same way they own physical products.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Amazon's Scrapped Stargate Show Featured Daniel Jackson Trapped in a Parallel Universe
articles.summary: Amazon's canned Stargate reboot would have starred Michael Shanks' fan-favorite character Daniel Jackson, trapped in a parallel universe.
articles.body:
Amazon's canned Stargate reboot would have starred Michael Shanks' fan-favorite character Daniel Jackson, trapped in a parallel universe.

Jackson confirmed he had been involved in the project this weekend at the Starfury: Ascension 2 convention in Birmingham, UK this weekend (thanks, Gateworld ) prompting more details on the project to be spilled via prolific Stargate fan podcast Dial the Gate .

Those details included the series' proposed setting: an alternate universe where numerous plot elements from past Stargate series would not have occurred. The idea here, it seems, would have been to offer a soft reboot of the franchise's continuity in order to cater for a new audience.

At the same time, the franchise's original Daniel Jackson would have been a regular character — giving returning fans a familiar face to tune in for, who still carried the knowledge of the original Stargate universe.

Later seasons had the potential to shift the series' narrative back to that Prime universe, it's reported, while the parallel universe setting would have allowed other Stargate veterans to make cameos, presumably as alt-universe versions of themselves.

Shanks' involvement in the project does not come as a surprise, following his past comments despairing at the series' abrupt cancellation by Amazon despite years of work and a triumphant public reveal . An initial report claimed that the show was scrapped due to fears it would not have appealled to anyone beyond the franchise's core audience — something that veteran Stargate writer Joseph Mallozzi, who had been working on the project, subsequently disputed.

Amazon is reportedly still interested in a future for the Stargate franchise, even if this specific revival series stays cancelled. But in a previous message to fans, Shanks suggested that this particular project represented fans' only hope of a revival built by former members of the Stargate SG-1 production team, and featuring members of its former cast.

Months later, and despite calls for fans to make their voices heard, there's no suggestion the series' cancellation will be reversed.

articles.title: Nintendo Developing New Smash Bros, Nintendogs, Mario Kart DLC With Star Fox, Leaker Claims
articles.summary: Nintendo is developing an all-new Super Smash Bros and Nintendogs, a notable leaker has claimed.
articles.body:
Nintendo is developing an all-new Super Smash Bros and Nintendogs, a notable leaker has claimed.

The details come from Malo932, who recently stated that Nintendo would hold two Direct presentations this week (correct), and who previously stated that a classic Star Fox , Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, and new Switch Sports would all be announced and launched this year (all correct too).

Word of a new Smash Bros. game is enormously exciting to the fighting game series' huge fanbase, though perhaps not a huge surprise considering how well Super Smash Bros. Ultimate sold on Nintendo Switch (at 38 million copies, it is the console's third-best selling game, behind Mario Kart 8 Deluxe and Animal Crossing: New Horizons). But one notable detail here is more surprising — that this is a new game, rather than a souped-up version of Ultimate. How the company plans to beat the Switch's hugely ambitious installment remains to be seen.

A fresh Nintendogs is another surprise, more than a decade on from Nintendogs + Cats, the franchise's last release back on 3DS in 2011.

Other claims made by Malo932, rounded up by Centro Leaks , include Mario Kart DLC coming next year featuring Fox McCloud, a new Star Fox Adventures game, a new Wario Land game, and a 2D Metroid. There's also mention of next year's widely-expected 3D Mario.

Many of these claims have subsequently been backed up by the more well-known Nintendo leaker NatetheHate, whose corroboration of the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake made headlines earlier this year. NatetheHate has a strong track record of Nintendo leaks, and previously also reported the Switch 2's reveal date accurately. Now, the company appears to have a second prolific source of leaks on its hands, too.

Nintendo will likely have been "furious" to see Zelda: Ocarina of Time and other surprises leak over the past six months, two former Nintendo staff members previously claimed. The console maker relies on its ability to surprise fans as a large part of its marketing. Instead, fans now believe they have a good idea of the company's upcoming product pipeline well into next year.

How many of these titles will make it into this week's pair of Nintendo Direct broadcasts , however, remains to be seen. Nintendo will use this week to lay out its plans for the Zelda series' 40th anniversary, with a deep dive into Ocarina of Time and a peek at the upcoming live-action Zelda movie both widely expected. Beyond that? Well, we'll just have to tune in and find out. As ever, IGN will be reporting on all of the official announcements as they happen.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: Bentley’s Torcal EV tries to balance authenticity with fake V8 sounds
articles.summary: Bentley’s Torcal EV is trying to expand the definition of craftsmanship with the new Torcal, the automaker’s first EV.
articles.body: Thanks to their ability to provide a smooth ride and quiet powertrain with ease, electric vehicles are a true shoo-in for the high-end luxury automotive segment. Rolls-Royce has the Spectre, Cadillac’s Celestiq is taking bespoke to a whole new level, and Mercedes has given the EQS the full Maybach treatment. From Volkswagen Auto Group, Bentley is just about to debut its 2027 Torcal, a spacious SUV that shares a platform with the electrified Porsche Cayenne. I recently got a quick ride in a heavily camouflaged preproduction Torcal as a way to experience it before its official debut toward the end of this month. Between this brute’s spacious interior, supple ride quality, and focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, all signs point to it not just being a viable competitor in the segment, but also characteristically Bentley. When I say heavily camouflaged, this not only covers (pun intended) the Torcal’s exterior, but the interior as well. Thick black cloth was draped over most of it, to the point of the engineers punching holes in the cloth for proper seatbelt usage. The exterior was rather deceiving, too; apparently they affixed false body paneling under the wrap so as not to fully spoil its overall shape and profile. Upon first glance, it seemed like Bentley took a page from Lucid’s Gravity by making it wider at the front than at the back—in the name of teardrop-resembling aerodynamics—but Martin Page, the Torcal’s product line director-slash-chauffeur for my ride, assured me that what I was seeing (or rather, trying to see) wouldn’t be production. [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: [Image: However, this enabled me to zero in closer on what I could feel and hear. Whether up front or in back, the Torcal is amply spacious, even though it’s noticeably smaller in size and shape than Bentley’s current Bentayga. Page explained the great lengths that engineers reached to ensure it had an isolating and tremendously smooth ride. Running off-the-shelf two-chamber air suspension — common in the rest of the brand’s lineup — would seemingly suffice with an EV’s inherently good chassis balance, but engineers took it a step further by carefully altering the flow of oil through its adaptive dampers. This means that the jump in ride and handling between Comfort and Sport modes is much more discernible. No matter the mode, it rode incredibly smoothly. Heavy focus was paid to the Torcal’s alignment, too, with steering that returns to and maintains center as confidently as possible. Diving deeper into signature Bentley characteristics, developing the best simulated engine note was high on the list of priorities. Inspiration came from the brand’s V8-powered Turbo R of the 1980s, except the track itself was recorded by a musician’s drum beat and mixed accordingly, rather than simply churned out from a synthesizer. “What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects,” Page shared. "“What we wanted to do throughout the car is maintain craftsmanship, not only in the materials but also in the way we execute the digital aspects.”" - Martin Page, Torcal’s product line director The reasoning behind this lies in hearing subtle imperfections, much like one would from an analogue internal combustion powertrain. Going one step further, the Torcal’s throttle tuning seemed to mimic a torquey V8 with progressive power delivery. In light of this, Page added that with this sound turned on, it gives occupants auditory cues to tie to the vehicle’s torque delivery, which is known to help reduce motion sickness. The sound has not yet been finalized and is still being finely tweaked at the time of this writing. I got a peek at the digital instrument cluster and center infotainment screen — Page had to observe the speed limit, after all. The image these display in the background is of a fine crystal decanter hand-cut by Cumbria Crystal with light shone through it. In Page’s words, this shows the natural refractions and reflections that you get from every one of the cuts. It’s another indication of the brand’s focus on craftsmanship in the digital age, albeit a subtle one. It’s also worth pointing out that Bentley takes net environmental impact seriously. “In this car we take sustainability to another level, we have clear targets for circular material and green aluminum,” Page shared. “The door cards are made with a natural fiber — not injection-molded plastic — that’s fully recyclable and fully sustainable.” [Media: Then, Bentley is working with fellow UK company Fox Brothers to offer a Merino wool interior option, not just as a lesser-taken route for comfort (Volvo’s done well with wool, too) but also as a sturdy, renewable material that will hold up to automotive use. Finally, the assembly plant in Crewe, England, has tough requirements for green energy use (namely solar) and other renewable practices. Output, battery, and charging specs are not carved into stone just yet. Power will be north of 800 hp and 700 lb ft of torque, and curb weight is estimated to be nearly 6,000 lbs. Page was quiet about battery size (though, expect it to mirror the Porsche’s 108 net kWh unit), and the targeted range is over 370 miles. With a peak charging rate of 400 kW, the brand is aiming for a 10–80 percent top-up in under 20 minutes, with 100 miles tacking on in as little as seven. “We’re trying to be authentic in the whole experience,” Page summed up as we headed back to the parking lot where I met him. The approach with the Torcal is to make a great Bentley first, and in the process of doing so, a great EV. It combines some already hashed-out tech from Volkswagen, but the brand is hoping its focus on craftsmanship and fine-tuning will attract discerning, well-heeled potential customers who want an electric luxury vehicle. Pricing hasn’t been announced yet, but it will be interesting to see how the Torcal is received after its full official unveiling. Images by Bentley

articles.title: Pokémon Go is Milking Mewtwo Too Hard, Fans Say, After a Lackluster Weekend Event Marred by More Server Issues
articles.summary: Mewtwo is being milked too hard, fans say, as Pokémon Go continues to capitalize on the creature's popularity and monetization potential.
articles.body:
There's a feeling that Mewtwo is being milked too hard, as Pokémon Go continues to capitalize on the creature's popularity and monetization potential.

The announcement of yet more Mewtwo coming to Pokémon Go later this year is being greeted with surprising apathy by fans, following a disappointing end of summer event this past weekend marred by yet more technical issues.

Mewtwo raids returned to Pokémon Go this summer after an extended absence, fuelling FOMO ahead of the long-awaited Mega Mewtwo X and Y release at Go Fest events in May, June, and July. Mega Mewtwo was also the star of the game's controversial New York anniversary event , disquiet over which preceded all players being gifted a unique 100% stat Mewtwo.

Go Fest Global in July, the game's biggest annual event, was essentially a Mega Mewtwo raid weekend for all players, which was fine — except for technical glitches that saw raiding impacted over a series of timezones across the world. A makeup event then took place in late July with more Mega Mewtwo offered.

All of which brings us to this past weekend, Go Fest: Mega Finale. There was some new content here — the addition of Mega Chesnaught, Mega Delphox, and Mega Greninja — but players could only acquire one of the three. Otherwise, the event was centered around (you guessed it) more Mewtwo. Mega Mewtwo X and Y returned yet again, alongside the creature's unique Armored Mewtwo version last seen in 2020.

Ahead of this weekend, Pokémon Go developer Scopely Explore stated that Armored Mewtwo would feature, but not yet be available in its Shiny version. Now, the developer has released an Avengers: Doomsday-style teaser video promising Armored Mewtwo will be back yet again later this year — which is when players widely expect its Shiny version to finally arrive, requiring more raiding to try and chase.

Armored Mewtwo isn’t done yet. Keep an eye to the sky for its return later this year. pic.twitter.com/at0UMAWEkB — Pokémon GO (@PokemonGoApp) September 7, 2026

Armored Mewtwo isn’t done yet. Keep an eye to the sky for its return later this year. pic.twitter.com/at0UMAWEkB

For players who may have spent the weekend raiding many Armored Mewtwo while it was available, the announcement it will be back again so soon is being seen as hasty at best, as accusations mount that the game is becoming too greedy, and against a backdrop of more complaints about technical issues.

Scopely Explore has acknowleged that raiding was impacted yesterday due to a "short network disruption that affected raids in the Americas," and gifted two raid passes as compensation. But while the company said it was continuing to monitor the issue, it also began directing further calls for recompense to its customer support team, with mixed reports of success.

"Armored Mewtwo will return in: give us more money," reads one response to the above teaser on top Pokémon Go fan reddit Silph Road . "Doing whatever it takes to milk the players left and right," reads another reply. "They've thrown so much Mewtwo at everyone that people are sick of it now," reads a third.

And the fact that yet another big Pokémon Go event has experienced technical issues has renewed calls for the game to change how it deducts raid passes from players' accounts, which differs from newer in-game battle currencies such as Max Particles and Link Charges. When a player begins a raid battle, their entry pass (free or paid) is taken as soon as the battle begins, which means it must be manually claimed back from the game's customer support team if the battle fails due to technical errors. For newer currencies, these are only deducted at the successful completion of a battle, meaning players don't lose out if something goes awry.

In another lengthy Silph Road thread, there are growing calls for this to finally change, and raid passes to only be deducted when the game detects a battle has successfully been completed. "This predatory practice by Niantic and then Scopely needs to stop," wrote one fan. "Today's debacle still would have resulted in a waste of people's time, which is unacceptable, but at least people's raid passes and money would not have been stolen by this widespread glitch. There is no player-friendly reason for raid passes to be consumed just for entering the raid."

IGN previously raised this issue with Pokémon Go senior producer John Funtanilla , who acknowledged that Max Particles and Link Charges had been built to be consumed following battles as a learning from raids — though there was no suggestion this would retroactively change for raid passes in the future.

"We really pushed for Max Particles not being consumed until you win," Funantilla said earlier this year. "Raid passes, meanwhile, are applied to the gym or Power Spot when you join the battle and that means until you win, you can keep trying. Max Particles and Link Charges [work similarly], so those will be consumed at the end of the battle once you win. That's a key learning that we wanted to carry forward.

"We're constantly talking with the player experience team for raiders, and they're looking at players trying to understand what problems are coming in. So we see that a lot and we try to build ways to reimburse if there's a crash, things like that. I understand it's not the best system, but we're trying to improve it with everything that we put in the game."

articles.title: Gary Oldman Says James Bond Has Been Cast — and He's Backing His Slow Horses Co-Star to Get the Job
articles.summary: Gary Oldman has said Amazon has finally decided which actor will play the new James Bond, and he’s backing his Slow Horses co-star.
articles.body:
Gary Oldman has said Amazon has finally decided which actor will play the new James Bond, and he’s backing his Slow Horses co-star.

Speaking to Canada’s The Morning Show to promote Slow Horses Season 6, Oldman teased 36-year-old Jack Lowden as Bond. Here’s exactly what Oldman said:

“Jack… it’s been rumored that he’s on the shortlist, or he’s one of… we’re gonna find out pretty soon, aren’t we? Because they have picked him. They have made their choice. But they have not announced it yet. So, my fingers are crossed for Jack.”

The Next James Bonds Who Never Played 007

Does that sound like Oldman is in the know here? Perhaps Jack Lowden let the good news slip during some downtime on-set. Perhaps this is just odd wording from Oldman, and he’s simply backing his colleague and doesn’t actually know. But he does sound convinced that a decision has been made, and an announcement is imminent.

In June, it was reported that Amazon had narrowed its shortlist of actors to play 007 in director Denis Villeneuve’s upcoming movie, with a second round of auditions set for August. The casting process officially began in the spring . At the time, Deadline reported that Harris Dickinson, Callum Turner, and Jacob Elordi "fit the prototype" of what producers were looking for from the next Bond. Amazon was said to be planning to make an announcement by the end of this year, with shooting set to kick off in 2027.

There's currently no release date for Bond 26, but presumably it will debut in 2028.

articles.title: As Onimusha: Way of the Sword Sells Over 1 Million Day One, Capcom Says It's 'Focusing on Re-Activating IPs That Haven’t Had a New Title Launch Recently'
articles.summary: Capcom looks like it has yet another hit video game on its hands, with Onimusha: Way of the Sword selling over 1 million copies on launch day.
articles.body:
Capcom looks like it has yet another hit video game on its hands, with Onimusha: Way of the Sword selling over 1 million copies on launch day.

The milestone pushed total Onimusha franchise sales over the 10 million units sold mark, 20 years after the last new game in the series came out.

“... through several marketing initiatives prior to launch, such as multiple demo releases and hands-on exhibitions, Capcom worked to expand awareness among a broad range of users, resulting in sales surpassing 1 million units on the day of its release,” Capcom said in a statement online .

Onimusha: Way of the Sword Gameplay Screenshots

But of most interest here is Capcom’s comment about repeating the Onimusha trick with other games from its back catalog.

“In addition to regularly releasing major new titles each year, Capcom is focusing on re-activating IPs that haven’t had a new title launch recently,” Capcom said. “The company is working to further maximize corporate value by leveraging its rich library of content, including this title.”

So, which series deserve the Onimusha treatment? I imagine there will be Dino Crisis fans screaming from the rafters here (Capcom is often asked about a new Dino Crisis game in interviews). We haven’t had a new Devil May Cry game in a while (Devil May Cry 5 came out in 2019), but I’m not sure I’d pop DMC in the same bucket as Onimusha, which hadn’t had a brand new game in two decades. Ace Attorney is another popular pick, as are Viewtiful Joe, Breath of Fire, and Lost Planet. Capcom has published a long list of games over the years. Take your pick.

Onimusha: Way of the Sword, meanwhile, continues Capcom’s hot streak, which has seen Pragmata establish itself as a potential franchise following strong sales. IGN’s Onimusha: Way of the Sword review returned a 10/10. We said: “Onimusha: Way of the Sword is an incredible action game with an excellent story to match.”

The Japanese games company has released hit after hit, from Monster Hunter to Resident Evil, Street Fighter to Dragon’s Dogma. What’s next? Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance is due out next year, as is Resident Evil Veronica and Mega Man: Dual Override. Further away is Okami 2, which is in the works at Hideki Kamiya's new studio, Clovers.

articles.title: Funko Reveals New Doctor Who Pop! Lineup, Featuring First-Ever Figures for River Song and the 15th Doctor
articles.summary: Funko has revealed a new lineup of Doctor Who figures, including David Tennant's 10th Doctor, Ncuti Gatwa's 15th Doctor, River Song, and a special Dalek collectible that's a rare chance find.
articles.body:
Heads up, Whovians: Funko has recently revealed its brand-new lineup of Doctor Who "Pop!" figures , all of which are now available to preorder. This includes new Funko figures for the 9th, 10th, 11th, and 15th Doctor, alongside a new figure for River Song.

Each of the new figures costs $14.99 and will be released on November 8, 2026 (excluding River Song, who will be available from January 30, 2027). There's also a premium "Rides Deluxe: Doctor Who — 10th Doctor with TARDIS" figure for $29.99 that features, well, the 10th Doctor with the TARDIS.

Rides Deluxe: Doctor Who - Tenth Doctor with Tardis

As per usual, David Tennant's 10th Doctor is getting the most attention from the new set and gets both of the most interesting new figure designs.

The Rides Deluxe figure is rather cool and features the Doctor leaning out of the TARDIS with his Sonic Screwdriver, and his iconic beige overcoat billowing in the wind (or maybe the Time Vortex?).

His new standard figure also recreates 10's iconic and emotional "I don't want to go..." regeneration scene (Vale Decum intensifies) . Or... according to its Funko description , this could also be depicting when the Doctor uses his regeneration energy to heal himself, but not change his appearance, during the Series 4 (2009) finale "Journey's End". I think it works for either, personally!

The 11th and 9th Doctor figures are a little more subdued and standard recreations of the characters. Both are still fairly good-looking figures, but do lack that bit of edge you can find in the 10th Doctor figures. Still, if you like them, don't let my grumpy opinions stop you!

It's also nice to see the first ever figures for both River Song and the 15th Doctor . Yet, we are lacking new Funko figures for Peter Capaldi's 12th Doctor and Jodie Whittaker's 13th. Perhaps we'll get to see something new for both at a later date, as it has been a while since we've gotten anything for either incarnation.

Rounding off the new lineup is the Funko exclusive "Bronze Dalek (Metallic)" for $14.99, and releasing on November 23, 2026. If you're lucky, you can also get a chance pull for a "Silver Metallic" classic looking Dalek instead. Fingers crossed, because this looks awesome.

While fans like myself will likely pick these up without second thought, Doctor Who has a pretty healthy Funko collecting scene, too, with older vaulted figures becoming increasingly tricky to find and some fetching significantly more than their original asking price on the secondary market.

I own a "12th Doctor with Guitar" figure , which is a good example, as it's one of those figures that's become considerably harder to find over the years, and can fetch for $35-$40 now on eBay.

Amazon has recently restocked a whole bunch of rare Pokémon TCG sets for Labor Day , and that includes the recently released First Partner Illustration Collection Series 3. It's available for just $33.99 from the major retailer right now, which is bang on market price at the likes of TCGplayer .

Pokémon TCG: First Partner Illustration Collection—Series 3

Considering Series 1 and 2 were easily going for $50+ not long after release, this is a pretty good offering in my honest opinion.

Pokémon TCG's First Partner Illustration Collection Series 3 is here as part of Pokémon's 30th anniversary celebrations, and it also marks the final entry in the First Partner Illustration Collection series.

Series 1 kicked things off by celebrating the classic Kanto (Gen 1), Sinnoh (Gen 4), and Alola (Gen 7) regions, while Series 2 moved on to Johto (Gen 2), Unova (Gen 5), and Galar (Gen 8).

Now, Series 3 rounds out the collection with first partner Pokémon from Hoenn (Gen 3), Kalos (Gen 6), and Paldea (Gen 9), giving collectors the chance to complete the full set of 27 starter Pokémon.

The current market price is hovering around $30-$35 before delivery, which makes Amazon one of the better places to pick these up, particularly if you're buying two or three at once. That's even more appealing if you're an Amazon Prime member and can take advantage of free, speedy delivery.

2 Pokémon TCG booster packs: Pulled from the Pitch Black and Chaos Rising expansions.

1 exclusive sticker sheet: Featuring the starter Pokémon from across the collection.

At around $34, this is arguably the best price we've seen for any of the First Partner Illustration Collection sets, but it's still more than double the original $14.99 MSRP.

articles.title: Why Brutality Is the Key to Making the Ultimate Wolverine Game
articles.summary: We dive into Logan's comic book history to explore why bloody brutality is the key to the ultimate Wolverine game.
articles.body:
There’s one thing that immediately jumps out when you watch even just a few seconds of Marvel’s Wolverine in action: it’s jaw-droppingly violent. There is so. Much. Blood. After a fight with a single enemy, Wolverine is drenched in gore and his own flesh is cut to ribbons. By a comfortable distance, Insomniac’s follow-up to its Spider-Man series is looking like the most violent superhero game we’ve ever seen.

While there will be a suite of violence customization settings for more squeamish players, it’s important to recognise that the immense violence on show here is not overkill. It’s actually completely in keeping with the character. The more you know about Wolverine, born as James Howlett, the more the hard-hitting bloodshed makes sense. This is not just violence for violence's sake. Let’s explore Wolverine’s complex comic book history to see why brutality is key to making the ultimate Wolverine game.

Comics (and particularly Marvel’s output) have a reputation for being kid-friendly, but most issues focused on Wolverine are hyper-violent and intended for more adult readers. There are staggering amounts of blood and death within those pages. In fact, one of Wolverine’s in-game abilities, “Rage Mode,” appears to be directly inspired by Logan’s antics in the 2020 comic series Wolverine: Black, White & Blood.

If your only experience of Logan comes via the X-Men films, then this may come as a surprise. While many of them are excellent, the movies present a much more family-friendly version of Wolverine. Hugh Jackman delivers plenty of the character’s trademark smart talk and attitude, but the majority of his appearances lack the visceral, cover-your-eyes kind of violence the character has delivered time and time again in the comics. Logan and Deadpool & Wolverine, both R-rated, get the closest to exploring his true nature, but even they still come in a few notches below the comics – yes, even that decapitation of Sabretooth is comparatively tame.

Stripping the violence way back makes sense from a film perspective (and a box-office one), but it robs the character of a core part of what makes him tick. Sanitizing the violence sanitizes the man himself. The comics are about a character who doesn’t just fight when necessary to protect his friends – there is rage in Wolverine. Violence isn’t just something he’s capable of, it’s an intrinsic part of him that he cannot live without. This is the guy who tore Hulk open from the inside (WOLVERINE: OLD MAN LOGAN GIANT SIZED 2009 #1), and that kind of untamed brutality is what a great Wolverine game needs—it must explore his extreme relationship with extreme violence.

That relationship began early. In Wolverine: Origin (2001), young James Howlett is described as “frail and sickly.” His father, John, is kind and loving, but his mother has become a recluse since her eldest son died of illness. You can practically feel the heartbreak in his face as John looks up at his mother’s balcony, hoping to catch even a glimpse of her. He’s a sweet, loving kid who wouldn’t hurt a fly – a far cry from the clawed killer he’ll one day become.

One moment changes everything: James watches a man called Logan kill his father with a shotgun. It’s a moment he can never return from. Completely and utterly overcome by rage, bone claws emerge from his hands for the first time, and he leaps at Logan, tearing apart his abdomen. It’s a natural, swift movement, as if James had been training for this his whole life. No longer the meek, sickly child: now, he is a brutal killer, so overpowered by grief that violence becomes the only answer. In the last frame of the story’s second issue, he kneels over the carnage he’s created, letting out a primal roar, a toxic mixture of grief and rage. He is no longer James. Now, he is Wolverine. The innocence he’s lost is gone for good.

This is an essential moment in understanding why Wolverine is prone to brutality. He’s predisposed to violence; when bad things happen, he doesn’t hesitate or hide, he gets brutal . He throws himself into action and doesn’t look back. This has remained consistent since he first appeared in Marvel comics in 1974. While many heroes refuse to kill, Wolverine has no issues taking a life. And so any game featuring Logan must channel a character that leaps into violence as an innate response.

There’s another layer to the moment in the comics, one that may just confirm that Wolverine’s violence is, in fact, innate. The man who murdered James’ father looks exactly like the adult Wolverine. Even his hair is identical. It’s never confirmed, but it’s highly insinuated that Logan is actually James’ biological father. This means that not only did young Wolverine kill his own father, but Wolverine’s violence isn’t just a physical response to tough situations. It’s a genetic one; brutality is embedded into his very DNA. It is, essentially, what makes Wolverine Wolverine.

In the 1960s, Wolverine found himself part of Team X, a black-ops military unit run by Weapon Plus and the C.I.A. Under their command, Wolverine is nothing more than a contract killer. He slices and dices his way through foes, being riddled with bullets and losing buckets of blood in one savage fight after the next.

What’s most disturbing about Wolverine’s time with Team X isn’t how many gallons of blood he’s spilled—that’s incalculable—but how he’s treated by those who run the team. Wolverine Origins (Issues #6-7, 2006) shows how, after each mission, soldiers would riddle him with bullets and then wait for his healing factor to revive him

Wolverine would also be forced to swallow pills containing Carbonadium, a highly radioactive metal that blocks his healing powers. That mutation doesn’t just knit Wolverine's flesh and bones back together and ensure his long life; as something of a survival mechanism, the healing factor also suppresses his memories. But Weapon Plus doesn’t want Wolverine’s memories suppressed: they want them completely erased. And so they torture the subdued mutant in an electric chair until he no longer remembers anything. They even attempt to strip Wolverine of his identity, referring to him as Experiment X. No longer a person in their eyes, Experiment X is designed to be the ultimate killing machine.

Marvel Presents explored the Weapon X program in great detail, depicting the countless painful tests Wolverine endured. The images within the comic’s pages are nearly as disturbing as the experiments themselves. Panels are drenched in bold oranges, pinks, reds, and purples, creating a nauseating feeling. Barry Windsor-Smith’s artwork oozes that raw, edgy quality of Marvel’s late 80s/early 90s aesthetic, augmented with elements of body horror maestro David Cronenberg – we see Wolverine submerged in tanks with endless tubes and needles stuck in him. An experience like this would haunt anyone for life. But when you torture someone who’s already lived so many violent lives, Weapon X only served to exacerbate Wolverine’s already frail psyche and violent behaviour.

Weapon X is the reason Wolverine has adamantium claws – the metal is bonded with his skeleton and thus his claws It’s an unbearably painful operation, but Weapon X presses on, unconcerned for Logan’s well-being and exclusively interested in making a super weapon. During the procedure, Wolverine wakes up, skin peeled off his body, screaming in agony, “What have you done to me?” It’s pure nightmare fuel, but it’s also perhaps the single image that best exemplifies why Wolverine is the way he is. Here is a man so tortured that he’s literally unrecognizable as a human being, stripped down to his savage bones.

In Wolverine’s world, violence consistently begets more violence. Eventually, the man who was once James Howlett finally snaps into his own consciousness and breaks out of the facility, utilising a level of violence we’d previously never seen from him. There’s a particular ruthlessness to his escape, tearing through soldiers to such a degree that blood saturates one panel after another.. He does it without a word – Weapon X has reduced him to nothing more than a feral beast. Even when he later regains consciousness and starts to recall his memories, that feral feeling never truly leaves him.

Because everyone treats him like a savage beast capable exclusively of brutality, that’s exactly how Wolverine sees himself. This is precisely what a Wolverine game needs to explore. What does it feel like to control a man who only sees himself as a savage brute, capable of killing men with the blink of an eye? What does it feel like to leap from one person to the next, claws extended, with the sole purpose of taking their life away? This is what Insomniac needs to examine for Wolverine’s story (and, by extension, gameplay) to be successful.

Wolverine’s saving grace comes when he joins Charles Xavier to become one of the X-Men. That’s where Logan truly begins to understand he’s more than just a killing machine. As part of the X-Men, he can finally serve the greater good, and he would start to become more of the warm, loving person he is—though not without his trademark edge. But Insomniac’s game takes place before Wolverine ever joined the X-Men. At this point in his life, all he knows is aggression.

Because Marvel comics have multiple timelines, it’s impossible to say at this point exactly where Insomniac’s Wolverine fits. What we do know is that the game finds Wolverine returning to Team X after three years away. The game’s version of the taskforce appears to include Jean Grey, who is not part of the team in the comics, so there will certainly be key differences. Wolverine also has adamantium claws, so it seems likely that it’ll touch on his experience with Weapon X, too. But since the game takes place before Wolverine ever joined the X-Men, at this point in his life, all he knows is aggression. That’s why the game’s violence is so necessary.

For better or worse, brutality is woven into Wolverine’s identity. And Insomniac’s latest appears to understand that better than any Wolverine or X-Men game we’ve played in the past. We can’t wait to see how it all unfolds on September 15.

articles.title: Lilly Wachowski Says 'I'm Kinda Done' With The Matrix, Reveals 'Complicated Situation' With The Matrix 5
articles.summary: Lilly Wachowski has said she’s “kinda done” with The Matrix, and suggested the recently announced The Matrix 5 may not move forward without the Wachowski’s blessing.
articles.body:
Lilly Wachowski has said she’s “kinda done” with The Matrix, and suggested the recently announced The Matrix 5 may not move forward without the Wachowski’s blessing.

Warner Bros. announced The Matrix 5 in 2024 , with The Martian and The Cabin in the Woods' Drew Goddard on board to write and direct. If it goes ahead, The Matrix 5 will be the first The Matrix movie not to have either Lana or Lilly Wachowski in the directing chair, although Lana Wachowski was reportedly down to executive produce.

“Drew came to Warner Bros. with a new idea that we all believe would be an incredible way to continue the Matrix world, by both honoring what Lana and Lilly began over 25-years ago and offering a unique perspective based on his own love of the series and characters," Warner Bros. Motion Pictures President of Production Jesse Ehrman said in a statement issued two years ago. "The entire team at Warner Bros. Discovery is thrilled for Drew to be making this new Matrix film, adding his vision to the cinematic canon the Wachowskis’ spent a quarter of a century building here at the studio.”

The Matrix Movies in (Chronological) Order

Fast forward to now, and Lilly Wachowski has poured cold water on excitement around The Matrix 5. “Warner Bros., they wanna make another thing,” she said in an interview on KCRW’s The Business , as reported by Variety . “They’re always gonna wanna make another thing. Personally, I don’t wanna play in that sandbox anymore. I’m kinda done.”

Wachowski went on to say that Goddard wants the Wachowski’s blessing before moving forward with The Matrix 5, which in turn has created a “complicated situation.”

“But there may be a thing that’s happening with Drew Goddard, and he doesn’t wanna go forward unless he gets our blessing,” she said. “And so, it becomes this complicated situation where, maybe we’re gonna stick our noses in a tiny bit and see how we feel, and if we wanna pass on our blessing to Drew or not. So, it could be something that’s coming down the road, but it’s still unknown.”

The groundbreaking The Matrix exploded onto the scene in March 1999, and was followed by The Matrix Reloaded in 2003, then The Matrix Revolutions in 2003. Nearly 20 years later, The Matrix Resurrections hit theaters in 2021. Lana Wachowski directed without Lilly, but Keanu Reeves and Carrie-Anne Moss reprised their iconic roles as Neo and Trinity, respectively.

The Matrix Resurrections saw mixed reviews and disappointed at the box office, grossing $157 million globally on a reported budget of $190 million. It's worth noting that it debuted while COVID-19 lockdowns were still affecting movie theaters, and it was one of the films to be released both in theaters and on HBO Max on the same day .

Nothing is known about The Matrix 5 other than Warner Bros. has announced it. If it does get made, will Reeves and Moss return once again? Based on Lilly Wachowski’s comments, it may be some time before we find out.

articles.title: GTA 6 Will Launch Digitally at Midnight Around the World, So Of Course Fans Are Already Planning to Set Their Console Locations to New Zealand
articles.summary: Rockstar will launch Grand Theft Auto 6 at midnight local time in most countries on November 19 — meaning some fans are already planning to adjust their console region and play early.
articles.body:
Rockstar will launch Grand Theft Auto 6 at midnight local time in most countries on November 19 — meaning some fans are already planning to adjust their console region and play early.

Rather than offering a fixed time worldwide, the midnight local rollout means players in New Zealand will get a roughly 20-hour headstart on Mexico and elsewhere in Central America.

Of course, there are no GTA 6 discs to get started with early — even though Rockstar's long-awaited release will arrive as an entirely single-player experience. While pre-loading will be available, the game itself will not unlock until your timezone's allotted window.

Even More GTA 6 Screenshots from Rockstar Games

Timestamps spotted on the PlayStation Store by GTAVice show 15 major release times for GTA 6 across the world's various timezones, beginning in New Zealand at 11am UTC on November 18, which is midnight on November 19 for our Kiwi friends.

If you're playing on Xbox Series X/S and want to adjust your console setting, this will be your earliest opportunity to play. If you have a PlayStation 5, this trick doesn't work — though you could technically play early with a separate New Zealand account, funded via a New Zealand gift card. (I guess this is one way GTA 6 actually plays better on Xbox .)

After New Zealand, the game's rollout then continues through timezones in Australia, Japan, India, through mainland Europe to the U.K., then to the U.S. — though at least here, all the country will get to play at midnight Eastern. So, if you're on the west coast, you'll get a few extra hours to play before bedtime (if you actually plan on going to sleep).

As a reminder, GTA 6 launches on November 19, just 72 days away. If you've preordered the game, you'll be able to start pre-loading from November 12, which is also when boxed copies (containing a digital download code) will ship. Rockstar is yet to say how much free space you'll need to get the game installed, but keep an eye on IGN for all of the details you'll need.

articles.title: Is GTA 6 Too Realistic for Its Own Good? Refueling Cars and Gun Restrictions Spark Debate
articles.summary: Early Grand Theft Auto 6 details have sparked debate about whether Rockstar Games' latest is too realistic for its own good.
articles.body:
Early Grand Theft Auto 6 details have sparked debate about whether Rockstar Games' latest is too realistic for its own good.

We've learned a lot about GTA 6 since its big extended look reveal. While the 13-year wait for Jason and Lucia's story already seems worth it for some, others fear Rockstar has taken its commitment to realistic gameplay a bit too seriously when it comes to its new open-world video game.

The studio is known for packing its games with details that fans could spend years combing through – and for better or worse, GTA 6 seems no different. Co-development lead Rob Nelson promised as much during a recent interview with content creator TGG . One element where the new Grand Theft Auto will differ from its predecessor involves how NPCs react to guns, with Nelson teasing that you can't just wander around with an RPG and expect zero pushback.

"The reactions are much more nuanced than before," he said. "So, if you've got a long gun on your back, you should be fine. If you've got one in your hand, people don't like it, and they react and start moving away from you. The more guns you carry and the way you carry them matters.

"If cops see you they will give you a warning. If you hold a long arm in both hands as though you are ready to fire it, things begin to escalate."

It certainly sounds more Red Dead Redemption 2 than Grand Theft Auto 5. Fans generally feel the 2013 GTA game thrives on mayhem, whereas the 2018 cowboy simulator found strength in its quiet, grounded moments. Nelson admitted that, in 2026, times have changed, explaining that Rockstar didn't "feel that works any longer at this resolution – with the behavioral sophistication we need from our population now."

"In GTA 5 you can pull out a shotgun from nowhere in front of people and they don't react," he elaborated. "That doesn't work here."

GTA 6 Reveal: 15 New Screenshots, Including 1 Exclusive on IGN

Even a slight shift toward a more realistic Vice City is something fans have expected from GTA 6 for some time, but that doesn't make Nelson's comments any less worth discussing. Should Rockstar lean on the cartoonish chaos GTA is known for, or sprinkle in the realism that made RDR2 special? That's the question many have found themselves asking the last few days.

"Next this game will make you file tax returns," one fan joked .

"I'm here for as full of an immersion as they can make," another argued , "RDR2 is the best game I've ever played and I love that they are making GTA 6 more like it."

Other fans fall somewhere in the middle, with one Reddit user pointing out that "At the point I pull out a gun I’m probably gonna do something worse than brandishing so this is fine."

remember carrying c4, rpgs, molotovs and like 10 guns at once in gta5 those days are over 😓 — kashmarth (@kashmarth) September 4, 2026

remember carrying c4, rpgs, molotovs and like 10 guns at once in gta5 those days are over 😓

When does a video game stop being a video game — emosxyual (@emosxyual) September 7, 2026

When does a video game stop being a video game

Rockstar is surely keenly aware of the balancing act it needs to pull off, but that didn't stop it from adding in more realistic elements. One mechanic present in other open-world sandbox games that will make its GTA debut in November will ask players to keep an eye on their car's gas. Yes, really.

In what leans more into the realism department, Nelson confirmed to TGG in a separate video that gas stations will allow players to repair and even refuel their vehicles. The YouTuber said filling up your car "typically isn't very expensive" and takes only about 10 seconds to do. It's no surprise to hear Rockstar already anticipated players being a bit torn when it asked players to bring car chases to a halt with a quick pitstop.

"That's pretty fast for a fill up," Nelson said when getting gas during TGG's preview event. "You can't complain about that!"

GTA 6 fans have, in fact, complained about that.

So in GTA 6 I have to: -eat -sleep -go to the gym -nurture my relationship -fill up my car with gas Isn’t the entire point of a video game to do things you can’t do in real life? This ultra-realism shit sounds exhausting — brick (@FreeMarketDog) September 3, 2026

So in GTA 6 I have to: -eat -sleep -go to the gym -nurture my relationship -fill up my car with gas Isn’t the entire point of a video game to do things you can’t do in real life? This ultra-realism shit sounds exhausting

imagine seeing this in gta6 pic.twitter.com/E4RJ6AKHl1 — 🏆 - Andy (@codedandunited) September 7, 2026

imagine seeing this in gta6 pic.twitter.com/E4RJ6AKHl1

I love that they added refueling to GTA 6 Imagine being chased by the cops and then suddenly your gas runs out near the swamps, so now you have to ditch the car and run through the swamps, dodging alligators AND cops. It's gonna result in so many unique gameplay moments! pic.twitter.com/87XIX6OpsC — Synth Potato🥔 (@SynthPotato) September 7, 2026

I love that they added refueling to GTA 6 Imagine being chased by the cops and then suddenly your gas runs out near the swamps, so now you have to ditch the car and run through the swamps, dodging alligators AND cops. It's gonna result in so many unique gameplay moments! pic.twitter.com/87XIX6OpsC

"Oh I can complain buddy," one Reddit user said . "I don't even know anything about this and I'm complaining already."

"It should make gameplay more interesting: you steal a car, run out of gas, have to continue on foot, try to find a gas station, or a new ride," another theorized . "More variation than driving indefinitely until you crash or escape. I'm into it."

"If I can’t pull up, standing their filling up whilst complaining about the price, then go inside to pay, standing behind someone who is buying 15 different chocolate bars and a s**tload of scratch cards then I don’t wanna play this realism simulator game!" one fan joked .

Rockstar's desire to drop players into a realistic Vice City extends beyond a few new gameplay mechanics and features. This version of the Miami-inspired sandbox will also feature what is promised to be the most realistic map players have explored in the series thus far. With more lifelike guns and characters comes potentially more realistic romance options , too. Some couples have reported that falling in love with Jason or Lucia, or heading to an in-game strip club, is grounds for a real-life break-up . Ouch.

But wait, there's more! GTA 6 will also track how Jason and Lucia are getting along in Vice City, including whether they've gotten enough beauty sleep in between heists. Nelson told TGG that players know whether the protagonists are well-rested enough, with sleep able to affect "regens of certain attributes." One mechanic Rockstar eventually cut for being too realistic would have had players purchasing groceries to restock their refrigerator.

"We are always trying to find the right balance between realism and ease of play," Nelson told Famitsu (translation by GamesRadar ). "Rather than just going to the fridge to grab a snack or visiting a restaurant just to roleplay, we want to give meaning to each action."

GTA 6 has (predictably) kicked up discourse months before its November 19 release date for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. That said, when it comes to the realistic elements in the game, one Reddit user nicely summed up how most will actually feel when they get their hands on the full release: "Just hope they remember to put the fun in. Realism is great, but if it's too tedious it'll be a bummer."

We'll know just how realistic gun restrictions, strip clubs, and fuel tanks will be when GTA 6 launches in a few months. While we wait, be sure to read up on IGN's interview and preview . You can also learn about the new PS5 controllers Rockstar announced last week.

articles.summary: Forza Horizon 6 is still planned to launch on PS5 this year, despite not having a firm release date yet.
articles.body:
Forza Horizon 6 is still planned to launch on PS5 this year, despite not having a firm release date yet.

Playground Games has confirmed it still plans to release Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 this year, following rumors that it might be delayed . Nothing else was shared about the port, but the clock is ticking for this new version.

"If you’re planning your trip to Discover Japan on PlayStation 5, stay tuned!" Playground said in a post today. "Forza Horizon 6 will be releasing on PS5 later this year, and you can add the game to your Wishlist on the PlayStation Store to be notified of availability."

September and October are loaded with big releases like Marvel's Wolverine and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , but there is enough difference in the audiences for these respective titles for Forza Horizon 6 to still succeed. November, however, is a different story. Launching Forza Horizon 6 on PS5 in November seems like a death wish given GTA 6 is set to dominate the industry upon its release. GTA 6 is expected to have an in-depth car customization system and races in addition to all of the other features one expects from GTA, making it hard to imagine players choosing Forza over GTA.

December may be more feasible, though the GTA 6 hype will still be very high and a hot item for the holiday season. It's hard to say, but Microsoft and Playground don't have too much time to build up to the PS5 release. Forza Horizon 5 was a massive hit on PlayStation 5, despite coming to the platform very late, so players will be attracted to it regardless.

Forza Horizon 6 is one of the biggest games of 2026 , which has been a very busy year for gaming. It's one of the best-selling games of the year and has garnered a ton of critical praise, including from IGN , which gave the game a 10/10.

"Technically, Forza Horizon 6 has not skipped a beat, and it runs like a titan," an excerpt from our review said. "Aesthetically, it’s the best-looking and best-sounding game Playground has produced to date, set in the most wonderfully realised map it’s ever crafted – full of dense, authentic details and stunning driving roads. It’s rewarding to explore, the campaign is well-paced with a great payoff, and I simply cannot stop playing."

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering's Hobbit Gift Bundles Are Back In Stock at Amazon
articles.summary: Save almost 20% and get a Collector Booster included with 9 Play Boosters, too.
articles.body:
In case you missed it, Magic: The Gathering has returned to Middle-Earth with some gusto. The Lord of the Rings set is widely regarded as one of the best Universes Beyond offerings yet, and The Hobbit is getting a pretty great reception from players, too.

As the set only launched recently, its Collector Boosters are harder to find than the Arkenstone in Smaug’s hoard of treasures, but Amazon has a “deal” that might get your attention.

There Is A Catch, Depending On Where You Stand

We say “deal” because, as with many things with this set right now, the Magic: The Gathering Hobbit Gift bundle is being sold for more than its MSRP.

In fact, Wizards says it should be $89.99, so $164 is a colossal price hike. And yet, the same bundle can be found for $200 elsewhere, or is simply sold out with no sign of returning.

We’re giving you this information up front because you’re a big Hobbit now and you can spend your money as you please, but this is still a discount of 18% on the same bundle purchased elsewhere. If you really want it, buy it; if you don’t want to spend that kind of money, we get it, but at least you’re informed.

So what’s the big draw? While it is true that you get 9 Play Boosters inside, the most valuable cards in the set are restricted to Collector Boosters. And in this bundle, you’ll find one (hopefully to rule them all).

Smaug, Wicked Worm (Borderless) (Surge Foil)

Smaug? Bard? Gandalf? What’ll it be? Well, that’s the point, really: you could open a whole bunch of neat rare cards, or you could pay your next month’s rent by pulling a Gleaming Splendor.

Aside from the ten total packs, you’ll also get 34 land cards that include full-art seasonal Hobbit lands that are exclusive to this set, and 10 full-art Middle-Earth Journey lands (honestly, these are so cool I’d probably frame them). There’s also a die inside and a box to keep everything in.

articles.title: Donegal GAA: McGuinness to continue as manager of Ulster county for another year
articles.summary: Jim McGuinness is reappointed as Donegal manager for a fourth year of his second spell in charge.
articles.body:
Jim McGuinness is to remain Donegal senior football manager for the 2027 season.

It will be his fourth year at the helm during his second stint in charge of the Ulster county.

Meanwhile Mickey McCann will continue to manage the county's senior hurlers for a further two years, having been in the role since 2018.

Donegal GAA confirmed the news on social media on Monday evening.

"Following a meeting of the County Committee, Donegal confirm the appointment of Michael McCann as Senior Hurling Manager for a two year term and Jim McGuinness as Senior Football manager for a one year term," it read.

During his second term in charge, McGuinness has helped guide Donegal to back-to-back Ulster titles in 2024 and 2025 and an All-Ireland final appearance in 2025.

The 53-year-old led Donegal to a Football League Division One final success over Kerry in March this year but the county's championship season was a disappointing one.

They were defeated by Down in the quarter-finals of the Ulster SFC and went down to Dublin after extra-time in Round 3 of the All-Ireland series.

McGuinness, who led Donegal to the All-Ireland in 2012 in his first spell as manager, initially returned on a three-year-deal with an option of a fourth.

articles.title: Sebastian Stan Half-Jokingly Pitched a 'Sicario-esque' Bucky Barnes Movie to MCU Boss Kevin Feige
articles.summary: The Winter Soldier himself, Sebastian Stan, recently pitched a "Sicario-esque" Bucky Barnes movie to Marvel Studios leadership.
articles.body:
The Winter Soldier himself, Sebastian Stan, recently pitched a " Sicario -esque" Bucky Barnes movie to Marvel Studios leadership.

When speaking to New York Magazine , Stan revealed that he pitched Kevin Feige on a solo Bucky Barnes film in the vein of Denis Villeneuve's 2015 movie, Sicario. The film would have been smaller in scope, with a tighter budget, and focused on a more personal mission for Bucky. Stan noted that he was "half-joking" with his pitch, but Feige responded well to it and said it sounds cool.

"We keep a real small budget," said Stan. "It's about a guy who thinks he recognizes someone from his past that had something to do with when, you know, he was brainwashed, and he gets obsessed with this person. He goes on a whole journey to try to figure out who this person is. It's a thriller."

Who Will Be the New Avengers in the MCU?

Although the MCU is intricately mapped out, the franchise has always had room to add in these kinds of unique passion projects. Ghost Rider, for instance, is something Ryan Gosling personally campaigned for and pitched to Marvel. The vision for the project was strong enough for Gosling to get the green light, and now, he'll make his MCU debut in summer 2028 . Whether Stan's passionate about pursuing this idea enough to make it a reality remains to be seen, but joke or not, the idea does sound like it could be a breath of fresh air for the franchise. It would also put a beloved character front and center after being relegated to a supporting character for over a decade.

Stan will reprise his role in Avengers: Doomsday this December, and he could play a role in next year's Secret Wars as well. Of course, Bucky Barnes could be killed off in either of these films, but death has never stopped a character from appearing again. Outside of multiversal/time travel shenanigans, Black Widow got a solo film after dying in Endgame . Marvel used it as an opportunity to fill a gap in the MCU timeline, and a similar thing could be done for Bucky should he be decimated by Doctor Doom.

Stan is also set to star in The Batman Part 2 , which he is filming until December. His role is being kept under wraps, but he's rumored to be Harvey Dent/Two-Face . Some have questioned the legitimacy of this rumor, as he's sporting a bald haircut in the film and Dent is known for his dashing appearance. He could sport a wig as Dent before being transformed into a more deformed, balding version of Two-Face, but we'll likely have to wait a while before knowing for sure.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Resonance Mod Brings Back Classic FF Character Ariana Grande
articles.summary: If you were upset to hear that pop star Ariana Grande wouldn't return in Final Fantasy Resonance, a new mod is here to save the day.
articles.body:
If you were upset to hear that pop star Ariana Grande wouldn't return in Final Fantasy Resonance , a new mod is here to save the day.

In case you were unaware, Square Enix's Final Fantasy Resonance will arrive as the long-running RPG franchise's first proper HD-2D game when it launches next month, and it also happens to be a bit of a remake. The game it's based on, Final Fantasy Brave Exvius , is a free-to-play game with turn-based gameplay that launched for iOS and Android devices in 2015 and shut down in 2025 – but what does that have to do with Ariana Grande?

The performer behind hits like "break up with your girlfriend, i'm bored," who also played Galinda in the recent Wicked films, isn't a newcomer for the Final Fantasy series. Grande actually joined Final Fantasy Brave Exvius in the form of pixelated characters – including one fit with her Dangerous Woman era bunny outfit – in 2017. The announcement (below) even detailed some in-game love for the pop star's song "Touch It," but when it comes to Final Fantasy Resonance, Grande's contribution to the series will be lost to time.

Producer Keisuke Nakashima recently confirmed to Kotaku that Grande "unfortunately" would not appear in the October Final Fantasy game. At the very least, it sounds like a decision Square Enix put some thought into.

"It’s also part of the worldview, you know?" he told the site. "Ariana Grande’s character would not fit within the vibe that we’ve created for Final Fantasy Resonance."

Modders, it seems, disagree. As spotlighted by the FFR Vision Studio mod (via Eurogamer ), Grande can feel right at home back in Final Fantasy Resonance along with a collection of other guest characters. That means you can add other names like Sora from Kingdom Hearts and 2B from Nier Automata to join the fight with only a few clicks.

Keep in mind that this is all more than one month before the game actually comes out. From Grande to Sora, these characters are only available to join Final Fantasy Resonance as part of its recently released demo. The demo does, however, allow players to carry their progress over to the full release, so it wouldn't be a surprise to see former Final Fantasy Brave Exvius characters show up in the launch build, too.

Final Fantasy Resonance launches for PC, Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X/S October 22, 2026. Until then, you can check out IGN's final preview for the game .
